not_said: The FGF PDF carries no date, version number or changelog anywhere in its 22 pages; the 2026-05-28 date used as the event date comes from OpenAI's news feed, not from the document itself.

The FGF does not present 50 fatalities / $1 billion as the only quantities in the document -- do not repeat that overclaim. The 2021 CBRN baseline year, the six-month/12-month/30-day cadences and the named standards (ISO 42001, ISO 27001 family, SOC 2 Type II) are also printed in it.

The FGF never states the effective dates of the TFAIA or the EU Code of Practice in its own text. The 2026-01-01 TFAIA effective date used in this article comes from the codified BPC chapter 25.1 text on leginfo (source 2), not from the FGF PDF.
The FGF never names a single OpenAI model, states which models are in scope, or says any model has crossed a risk tier.

The FGF's own text does not state the 10^26 compute figure or the $500 million revenue figure; those numbers are stated only in SB 53's codified text (source 2), and must be attributed to the statute, not to OpenAI.

The FGF does not name any external expert, third-party evaluator or red-teaming organisation, and does not commit to mandatory external review; its wording is 'we may solicit and obtain input from external experts'.
The FGF says nothing about consumer-facing products, prices, plans, regions or languages, and does not claim to change anything a user sees in ChatGPT.
The FGF mentions no jurisdiction other than California/the United States and the EU/Ireland. Taiwan, Japan, Korea, the UK and China are not mentioned anywhere in it.

The FGF does not mention penalties, fines or enforcement consequences. The $1,000,000-per-violation figure and the Attorney General's exclusive right of action are stated only in SB 53 (source 2), not in OpenAI's document.
The FGF gives no tier table for harmful manipulation; three of the four categories (cyber offense, CBRN, loss of control) have numbered tiers, harmful manipulation does not.
Neither the FGF nor the codified TFAIA chapter states that any regulator approved, endorsed or certified OpenAI's framework.

editorial_brief: 讀者：在台灣用 ChatGPT 的一般使用者，以及公司裡要判斷『這家 AI 廠商可不可以信』的人。角度：2026 年 5 月 28 日 OpenAI 公開一份 22 頁的 Frontier Governance Framework，這不是新的安全承諾，而是一份同時交給加州與歐盟主管機關看的合規文件。五節骨架：(1) 5/28 發生了什麼、FGF 同時對應哪兩套法規；(2) 50 人、10 億美元的門檻其實是加州 SB 53 的法定定義，附三個排除與股權除外，並與 OpenAI 自己 Preparedness Framework 的更高門檻對照（表格收尾）；(3) 三級風險分級實際寫了什麼、CBRN 的 2021 年基準是什麼意思、有害操弄為何還沒有分級表（圖解收尾）；(4) 公布之後誰能追蹤：12 個月總檢視、30 天內公布異動、受歐盟法規範模型的 6 個月模型報告更新、SB 53 的年度檢視與最高 100 萬美元罰鍰；(5) 文件沒提到台灣、介面沒有變化、讀者怎麼自己查證。topics 定為 ["ai","ai-news"]（治理框架屬公司層級新聞，不掛 software；不掛 finance，即使題目談的是罰鍰與門檻）。兩個 link：第一個是索引 ai-news-2026-january-september-index（text 逐字照抄協調者給的新標題）；第二個是 ai-news-gpt-55-instant-20260505（本文撰寫時該篇尚未成稿，text 暫填研究紀錄裡建議的方向標題，等協調者事後用工具統一換成正式標題）。刻意不談：歐盟 AI 法第 50 條標示義務（ai-news-eu-transparency-20260802 的主題）、前沿 AI 放慢與否的價值辯論（ai-news-pace-the-frontier-20260912 的主題）、OpenAI 募資與 S-1、FGF 與 PF 風險分級文字的逐字重疊（見 must_add，本輪未寫入正文）。
must_not_write: Do not call this a new safety policy or say OpenAI 'tightened' its rules -- the FGF text itself frames it as overlapping with the existing Preparedness Framework and documenting compliance with two laws.

Do not attribute the '50 fatalities / $1 billion' figures to OpenAI's own risk appetite; they are California SB 53's statutory definition, and the article says so in the same sentence each time it uses them.

Do not say the framework was approved, accepted, endorsed or certified by the European Commission, the AI Office, the California Attorney General or the Office of Emergency Services -- no source says that.
Do not write 'we tested' or 'we verified' about any capability, tier or security claim; all such claims are OpenAI's own wording, attributed as 'OpenAI 表示' / 'FGF 文件寫道'.
Do not treat this as investment or corporate news, and do not connect it to OpenAI's fundraising or any S-1 filing -- AI vertical only, no finance topic, no investment framing.
Do not tell readers in Taiwan that any of these rules protect them; the TFAIA is Californian and the Code of Practice is EU, and the article says explicitly that neither names Taiwan.

Do not re-explain the EU AI Act's Article 50 chatbot/deepfake labelling rules -- that is the existing article ai-news-eu-transparency-20260802's subject, a different part of the same law, and this article does not mention it at all.
Do not re-argue whether frontier AI should be slowed down -- that is ai-news-pace-the-frontier-20260912's subject; this article only links to it, it does not restate its argument.
Do not quote '27/7/365' and do not silently correct it to 24/7 -- leave the figure out entirely, which this article does.
Do not invent a fifth risk category or a harmful-manipulation tier table, and do not state numeric scores for any tier -- the FGF publishes none.
Do not cite openai.com/index/openai-frontier-governance-framework/ (or any /index/ page) as a fetched source -- it returns HTTP 403 and was not read by this writer.
